What has changed is that a genuine preregistration was located outside the repository: vault card `bm3-secondary-ablation-decide.md` (created 2026-07-03, in `/mnt/c/Users/ThinkPad/Obsidian Vault/`), corroborated word-for-word by an independent `log.md` entry dated the same day, both predating the grid's 2026-07-03T10:34 start by the ordering documented in `prereg_provenance.md`. The automated reviewer could not have found this: `run_codex_review()` in `/home/jeffwork/exp/physics-mechanism/orchestrate.py` passes the reviewer only the card's RUBRIC section plus the git workdir's contents, never the card's TASK section (where the concrete 8pp/[3,8)pp/collapse-to-s4d rule lives) and never the external vault path. That is a structural scope limitation of the review harness, not a mistake by the reviewer. Given the reviewer's own stated fallback -- apply an already-registered Delta-pp threshold if one is found to exist -- the correct resolution is to materialize that provenance (prereg_provenance.md) and mechanically apply the card's actual rule to the already-frozen aggregate outputs (secondary_decision.json in this directory), without rerunning the grid, without changing any aggregate value, and without touching the 175 raw cells. That is what this directory does. Rerunning the grid, as a literal reading of the reviewer's REVISE might suggest absent this new information, is not necessary once the pre-existing valid registration is on the record.
